18.4 The OTel Demo Application — Astronomy Shop

The official CNCF demo (github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo) showcases OTel across 12+ microservices in 12+ different languages — each instrumented with its native OTel SDK. It's the best way to see how OTel looks in YOUR language and how context propagation works across a polyglot system.

🌐 Languages in Demo

Python, Go, Java, JavaScript, C++, Ruby, Rust, Kotlin, TypeScript, .NET, PHP — all using OTel in their native SDK.

📚 What You'll Learn

Manual vs auto-instrumentation per language, Collector config for polyglot envs, context propagation across 12 services, realistic semantic conventions.

18.5 Choosing the Right Backend — Decision Framework

6 Questions to Ask (In Order)
#QuestionIf SmallIf Large
1Scale? Spans/sec<1K/s: Any backend>100K/s: Tempo/Mimir or Commercial
2Retention? How long?<7 days: Any>90 days: Object storage (S3)
3Team Size? Who operates?1-3: Managed (Grafana Cloud, Datadog)10+: Self-host LGTM viable
4Budget? Monthly spend<$100: Self-host LGTM or free tier>$2000: Datadog, Dynatrace Enterprise
5Existing Tools?Greenfield → LGTM (free, OTLP-native)Splunk shop → Splunk Observability
6High Cardinality?No → Any backendYes → Honeycomb (built for it)

18.6 Cost Considerations — Telemetry Data Volume

ScenarioTrafficMonthly SpansStorageEst. Cost (LGTM)
Dev10 req/s, 8h/day~2.8M~14 GB~$0 (free tier)
Production100 req/s, 24/7, 10% sampling~2.6M~10 GB~$50/mo
High Scale1000 req/s, 24/7, 1% sampling~2.6M~10 GB~$100/mo
High Scale (100%)1000 req/s, 24/7~260M~1 TB~$500+/mo
⚠️ Sampling is cost-critical at scale: 1000 req/s at 100% sampling = 260M spans/month = ~1 TB. At 1% sampling = 2.6M spans = ~10 GB. That's a 100x cost difference!

18.7 Hands-On: Switch anihpj from Jaeger to Grafana Tempo

1
Verify Current State
Traces visible in Jaeger at localhost:16686. anihpj sends OTLP → Collector → Jaeger.
2
Start Tempo
docker run -d --name tempo -p 3200:3200 -p 4317:4317 grafana/tempo:latest
3
Edit ONE line
Change Collector config: endpoint: jaeger:4317 → endpoint: tempo:4317
4
Restart Collector
docker restart otel-collector
5
Verify in Grafana
Add Tempo data source → Query: {resource.service.name="anihpj"}
6
PROVE Zero Code Changes
Check anihpj: settings.py unchanged, views.py unchanged, env vars unchanged. Only 1 YAML line changed!

18.X Vendor Backend Selection — The 6-Question Framework

Choosing an observability backend is one of the most consequential decisions. The OTCA exam tests matching scenarios to the right backend.

The 6-Question Backend Decision Framework
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │          THE 6 QUESTIONS THAT DETERMINE YOUR OBSERVABILITY BACKEND         │
  │                                                                          │
  │  Q1: SCALE — How many spans/sec?                                         │
  │     < 10K/sec → Any backend. > 100K/sec → Tempo (S3, no indexing)      │
  │                                                                          │
  │  Q2: RETENTION — How long? <7d → Jaeger+ES. >30d → Tempo/Loki (S3)    │
  │                                                                          │
  │  Q3: TEAM SIZE — 1-3 people → SaaS. 5+ SREs → Self-hosted LGTM          │
  │                                                                          │
  │  Q4: BUDGET — $0 → LGTM self-hosted or Grafana Cloud free tier          │
  │     $500+ → Grafana Cloud paid. $5000+ → Datadog/Dynatrace/Splunk       │
  │                                                                          │
  │  Q5: EXISTING TOOLS — Prometheus → LGTM. Datadog → Datadog APM.          │
  │     ELK → Jaeger (ES storage) or Elastic APM                             │
  │                                                                          │
  │  Q6: HIGH CARDINALITY? YES → Honeycomb or Tempo+TraceQL. NO → Any.       │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
💡 OTCA Exam: Backend Scenarios

"A startup with 3 engineers, $0 budget, 500 req/s." → Self-hosted LGTM or Grafana Cloud free tier. "Enterprise, 500 microservices, existing Datadog." → Datadog APM with OTel Collector feeding OTLP. Match backend to constraints: budget, team size, scale, existing tools, cardinality needs.

📝 OTCA Practice Questions — Chapter 18

Q1
What does LGTM stand for in the Grafana stack?
Show Answer
Answer
  L = Loki      → Log aggregation (LogQL, S3-backed)
  G = Grafana   → Unified visualization & alerting
  T = Tempo     → Distributed tracing (TraceQL, S3-backed)
  M = Mimir     → Long-term metrics (PromQL, S3-backed)
  
  + P = Pyroscope → Continuous profiling (emerging 4th signal)
  
  All open source. All OTLP-native. All S3-backed = cheap at scale.
Explanation

The LGTM stack is the open-source observability platform from Grafana Labs. Every component speaks OTLP natively. S3-compatible object storage makes it ~10x cheaper than SSD-backed alternatives at scale. OTCA exam may ask about the components of the LGTM stack.

Q2
What is Honeycomb's unique differentiator?
Show Answer
Answer
  Honeycomb differentiators:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 🫧 BubbleUp — statistical analysis                   │
  │    Compares slow traces vs fast traces               │
  │    Identifies "what's different?" automatically      │
  │    WITHOUT you writing any query                      │
  │                                                      │
  │ 🔢 HIGH CARDINALITY — query by ANY field             │
  │    user_id, trace_id, session_id, cart_id            │
  │    While Prometheus limits labels to ~10 values      │
  │    Honeycomb handles millions of unique values        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Explanation

Honeycomb is observability-first (not APM). Its core innovation is BubbleUp — it statistically compares traces to find anomalies without you writing queries. It also supports high-cardinality queries that would OOM Prometheus. Best for teams that want "unknown unknowns" discovery.

Q3
How does OTel enable backend switching without code changes?
Show Answer
Answer
  SWITCHING BACKENDS — ONE LINE CHANGES:
  
  export:
    otlp:
      endpoint: jaeger:4317     # Before
      endpoint: tempo:4317      # After (ONLY THIS CHANGES)
  
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ anihpj: ZERO changes                                │
  │ settings.py → unchanged                              │
  │ views.py    → unchanged                              │
  │ env vars    → unchanged                              │
  │                                                      │
  │ Docker restart otel-collector → DONE                 │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  "Instrument once. Export anywhere. Forever."
Explanation

The app never knows which backend receives the data. It always sends OTLP to the Collector. Only the Collector's YAML config changes. This eliminates vendor lock-in — the core OTel value proposition that the OTCA exam will test.

Q4
What is the recommended backend for a team with a $0 budget?
Show Answer
Answer

  │   docker-compose up (Tempo + Loki + Mimir + Grafana) │
  │   Cost: $0 (just your server costs)                  │
  │                                                      │
  │ Option 2: Grafana Cloud Free Tier                    │
  │   10,000 metrics series                              │
  │   50 GB traces                                       │
  │   50 GB logs                                         │
  │   Cost: $0/month                                     │

Explanation

The Grafana Cloud free tier is surprisingly generous — enough for most development and small production workloads. Self-hosted LGTM costs only your infrastructure (a modest VM or K8s cluster). Both options are fully OTLP-native.

Q5
Why are Tempo and Loki cheaper than Jaeger and Elasticsearch at scale?
Show Answer
Answer
  STORAGE COST COMPARISON:
  ┌──────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────┐
  │ Jaeger + ES      │ Tempo + S3       │ Loki + S3        │
  ├──────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────┤
  │ SSD storage      │ Object storage   │ Object storage   │
  │ ~$0.10/GB/month  │ ~$0.023/GB/month │ ~$0.023/GB/month │
  │ Full-text index  │ NO span indexing │ NO log indexing  │
  │                  │ (label-based)    │ (label-based)    │
  │ 10TB = $1000/mo  │ 10TB = $230/mo   │ 10TB = $230/mo   │
  └──────────────────┴──────────────────┴──────────────────┘
  
  Key insight: Object storage is ~4-10x cheaper
  Label-based lookup avoids expensive full-text indexing
Explanation

Tempo and Loki use S3/GCS object storage instead of SSD-backed databases. They don't index every span attribute or log field — instead they use label-based lookup (like Prometheus). This makes them massively cheaper at scale. OTCA exam: know that object storage = cheaper long-term retention.

Q8
What is the 6th question in the backend decision framework?
Show Answer
Answer
  BACKEND DECISION FRAMEWORK (6 questions in order):
  ┌─────┬─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┐
  │ 1   │ SCALE?              │ Spans/sec → sizing           │
  │ 2   │ RETENTION?          │ How long → storage           │
  │ 3   │ TEAM SIZE?          │ Who operates? → managed      │
  │ 4   │ BUDGET?             │ Monthly spend → options      │
  │ 5   │ EXISTING TOOLS?     │ What's already deployed?     │
  │ 6   │ HIGH CARDINALITY?   │ Query by user_id? ← ANSWER   │
  │     │                     │ YES → Honeycomb or Tempo     │
  │     │                     │ NO  → Any backend works      │
  └─────┴─────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
Explanation

Question 6 determines whether you need Honeycomb (built for high cardinality) or can use any backend. Most backends struggle with high-cardinality queries (user_id, trace_id). If you need to query by these fields, Honeycomb or Tempo (TraceQL) are your best options.

Q9
How much does sampling reduce cost?
Show Answer
Answer
  SAMPLING COST IMPACT (1000 req/s, 24/7):
  ┌─────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐
  │ Sampling %  │ Monthly Spans│ Storage      │ Cost/Impact   │
  ├─────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┤
  │ 100%        │ 260M         │ ~1 TB        │ $$$$$         │
  │ 10%         │ 26M          │ ~100 GB      │ 90% savings   │
  │ 1%          │ 2.6M         │ ~10 GB       │ 99% savings   │
  └─────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┘
  
  Config: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=traceidratio
          OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.01  # 1%
  
  ⚠️ Sampling applies to TRACES only (not metrics/logs)
Explanation

Sampling is the #1 cost lever for traces. 100% → 10% = ~90% cost reduction. At 1000 req/s, 100% sampling = 260M spans (~1TB) per month. At 1% sampling = 2.6M spans (~10GB). OTCA exam: sampling is for TRACES only — metrics are aggregated, logs are not sampled.

⚠️ Common Mistakes — Vendor Backends

  • Vendor lock-in fear: OTel eliminates this — instrument once, switch backends anytime
  • Overpaying for traces: 100% sampling at scale = extreme costs. Use 1-10% sampling
  • Choosing wrong storage: SSD (Elasticsearch) for long retention = expensive. S3 (Tempo/Loki) = cheap
  • Ignoring free tiers: Grafana Cloud free tier covers most dev/small-prod needs

Chapter: Security, Sensitive Data & OpAMP — Production Best Practices 🔴 Production

Security, Sensitive Data & OpAMP — Protecting Your Observability Pipeline

Security in observability is often overlooked — but telemetry data contains PII, API keys, SQL queries, and network paths. This chapter covers what the official OpenTelemetry documentation recommends for security, handling sensitive data, and the OpAMP protocol for managing Collector fleets at scale.

Security 1: Collector Configuration Best Practices

The Collector is the central routing layer — if compromised, ALL telemetry is at risk. The official OTel docs recommend these configuration best practices:

Collector Security — Defense in Depth
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │              COLLECTOR SECURITY — LAYERED DEFENSE                          │
  │                                                                          │
  │  LAYER 1: TRANSPORT SECURITY (TLS/mTLS)                                   │
  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
  │  │ SDK → Collector: TLS (encrypt data in transit)                     │  │
  │  │ Collector → Backend: TLS + optional mTLS (mutual auth)            │  │
  │  │                                                                    │  │
  │  │ receivers:                                                         │  │
  │  │   otlp:                                                            │  │
  │  │     protocols:                                                     │  │
  │  │       grpc:                                                        │  │
  │  │         tls:                                                       │  │
  │  │           cert_file: /certs/server.crt    ← Server certificate     │  │
  │  │           key_file: /certs/server.key                              │  │
  │  │           client_ca_file: /certs/ca.crt   ← Verify clients (mTLS)  │  │
  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
  │                                                                          │
  │  LAYER 2: AUTHENTICATION & AUTHORIZATION                                  │
  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
  │  │ Bearer Token Auth:                                                 │  │
  │  │   receivers:                                                       │  │
  │  │     otlp:                                                          │  │
  │  │       grpc:                                                        │  │
  │  │         auth:                                                      │  │
  │  │           authenticator: bearertokenauth                           │  │
  │  │                                                                    │  │
  │  │ Headers-based Auth (for SaaS backends):                            │  │
  │  │   exporters:                                                       │  │
  │  │     otlp:                                                          │  │
  │  │       headers:                                                     │  │
  │  │         "Authorization": "Bearer ${GRAFANA_CLOUD_TOKEN}"           │  │
  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
  │                                                                          │
  │  LAYER 3: DATA PROTECTION (Sensitive Data Handling)                       │
  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
  │  │ Filter out sensitive attributes BEFORE export:                     │  │
  │  │   processors:                                                      │  │
  │  │     attributes:                                                    │  │
  │  │       actions:                                                     │  │
  │  │         - key: user.password         action: delete                │  │
  │  │         - key: user.email            action: hash                  │  │
  │  │         - key: credit_card           action: delete                │  │
  │  │         - key: db.statement           action: delete  ← SQL query! │  │
  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
  │                                                                          │
  │  LAYER 4: RESOURCE PROTECTION (Rate Limiting, DoS Prevention)             │
  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
  │  │   processors:                                                      │  │
  │  │     memory_limiter:       ← Prevents OOM (DoS vector)              │  │
  │  │       limit_mib: 512                                               │  │
  │  │     batch:                ← Reduces backend load                   │  │
  │  │       send_batch_size: 8192                                        │  │
  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
⚠️ The #1 Security Mistake: Exposing SQL Queries in Spans

Auto-instrumentation for database drivers captures the FULL SQL query (including parameter values) as db.statement. If a user logs in with password=secret123, that password is now in your tracing backend — searchable by anyone with access. Always sanitize db.statement using the attributes processor to either delete it or redact parameters. This is a critical production security concern.

Security 2: Handling Sensitive Data in Telemetry

The official OTel documentation has an entire section on handling sensitive data. Telemetry can unintentionally capture PII (Personally Identifiable Information), credentials, and internal network topology.

Sensitive Data TypeHow It Leaks Into TelemetryMitigation
Passwords/API KeysHTTP headers (Authorization), URL query paramsFilter processor: delete attributes matching "Authorization", "api_key"
PII (emails, names, IDs)Span attributes (user.email, user.name)Hash or delete: action: hash (one-way) or action: delete
SQL Queriesdb.statement attribute (INCLUDES values!)Delete db.statement; keep db.operation only
Network Topologynet.peer.ip, host.name, k8s.pod.nameKeep for debugging; restrict access to backend
Request Bodieshttp.request.body (if enabled)NEVER enable body capture in production
YAML — Redacting Sensitive Data in the Collector
processors:
  attributes:
    actions:
      # DELETE: Completely remove sensitive attributes
      - key: db.statement
        action: delete
      - key: http.request.header.Authorization
        action: delete
      - key: user.password
        action: delete
      
      # HASH: Keep for debugging but anonymize (SHA256)
      - key: user.email
        action: hash
      - key: user.id
        action: hash
      
      # UPDATE: Replace with redacted value
      - key: credit_card
        action: update
        value: "[REDACTED]"

OpAMP — Open Agent Management Protocol

OpAMP is an official OTel specification for remotely managing large fleets of data collection Agents (like the OTel Collector). If you have 1,000 Collectors across 10 Kubernetes clusters, OpAMP lets you manage them all from a central Server.

OpAMP Architecture — Centralized Collector Fleet Management
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │              OPAMP — MANAGING COLLECTOR FLEETS AT SCALE                    │
  │                                                                          │
  │                      ┌─────────────────┐                                  │
  │                      │   OpAMP Server   │  ← Central management plane     │
  │                      │   (UI + API +    │                                  │
  │                      │    Config Store) │                                  │
  │                      └────────┬────────┘                                  │
  │                               │                                           │
  │          ┌────────────────────┼────────────────────┐                      │
  │          │                    │                    │                      │
  │          ▼                    ▼                    ▼                      │
  │  ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐                │
  │  │ K8s Cluster 1│    │ K8s Cluster 2│    │ K8s Cluster N│                │
  │  │ ┌──────────┐ │    │ ┌──────────┐ │    │ ┌──────────┐ │                │
  │  │ │Collector │ │    │ │Collector │ │    │ │Collector │ │                │
  │  │ │+ OpAMP   │ │    │ │+ OpAMP   │ │    │ │+ OpAMP   │ │                │
  │  │ │ Client   │ │    │ │ Client   │ │    │ │ Client   │ │                │
  │  │ └──────────┘ │    │ └──────────┘ │    │ └──────────┘ │                │
  │  └──────────────┘    └──────────────┘    └──────────────┘                │
  │                                                                          │
  │  OpAMP CAPABILITIES:                                                      │
  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
  │  │ ✅ Remote Configuration — Push collector config updates centrally  │  │
  │  │ ✅ Status Reporting — Each Collector reports health + metrics       │  │
  │  │ ✅ Package Management — Download/update Collector binaries         │  │
  │  │ ✅ Connection Settings — Rotate TLS certs, change endpoints        │  │
  │  │ ✅ Heartbeating — Detect dead Collectors automatically             │  │
  │  │ ✅ Auto-Upgrade — Push new Collector versions to fleet             │  │
  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
  │                                                                          │
  │  Protocol: WebSocket (full-duplex) or HTTP (polling)                     │
  │  Default port: 4320                                                      │
  │  Default path: /v1/opamp                                                 │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
🔧 When You Need OpAMP
  • Managing 50+ Collectors across multiple clusters
  • Need to push config changes to all Collectors at once
  • Want centralized health monitoring of Collectors
  • Need to rotate TLS certificates fleet-wide
  • Automated Collector version upgrades
✅ When You DON'T Need OpAMP
  • Single Collector deployment
  • Using Kubernetes ConfigMaps for Collector config
  • Using GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux) for config management
  • Small team managing < 10 Collectors
📖 OTCA Relevance

While OpAMP is NOT a core OTCA exam topic, knowing it exists and what it does demonstrates understanding of the broader OTel ecosystem. The exam focuses more on Collector configuration and pipeline management, which OpAMP helps with at scale. The security topics above (TLS, auth, sensitive data handling) ARE relevant to the OTCA, particularly in D4 (Maintaining & Debugging Pipelines).

📋 Part 4 Exam Quick Reference

ConceptKey PointsOTCA Weight
Logs Bridge APIBridges existing logger (NOT replaces). trace_id auto-injected. Same OTLP pipeline as traces/metrics.MEDIUM
CollectorOptional but recommended. Agent (per-node) → Gateway (centralized). otelcol-contrib for production.HIGH
Batch & Memory LimiterALWAYS use in production. Batch: 200ms/8192. Memory: 512 MiB limit + spike limit.HIGH
OTLP ExporterStandard exporter for all signals. gRPC:4317, HTTP:4318. Always prefer over legacy exporters.HIGH
Backend SwitchingChange 1 YAML line in Collector. ZERO app code changes. "Instrument once, export anywhere."MEDIUM
LGTM StackLoki (logs), Grafana (viz), Tempo (traces), Mimir (metrics). All OSS, OTLP-native, S3-backed.MEDIUM

⚠️ Top 5 Part 4 Exam Traps

  • OTel replaces my logger: NO — it BRIDGES. You still use your existing logging library.
  • Collector is required: NO — it's optional but recommended for production.
  • Native Jaeger exporter is preferred: NO — OTLP is the standard. Jaeger accepts OTLP natively.
  • 100% sampling is free: NO — 100% sampling at scale = extreme costs. Use 1-10%.
  • Unstructured logs are fine: NO — structured JSON is essential for queryability and correlation.

19.3 Key Concepts to Memorize

a) OTel Architecture: API → SDK → Collector → OTLP

API = interfaces (no implementation). SDK = implementation (sampling, batching, exporting). Collector = standalone pipeline (receive, process, export). OTLP = wire protocol (gRPC:4317, HTTP:4318). TracerProvider→Tracer→Span. MeterProvider→Meter→Instrument. LoggerProvider→Logger→LogRecord.

b) Signal Types: Traces, Metrics, Logs

Traces: Spans with trace_id + span_id + parent_span_id. 5 Span Kinds (SERVER/CLIENT/INTERNAL/PRODUCER/CONSUMER). Metrics: 6 Instruments (Counter, UpDownCounter, Histogram, ObservableGauge, ObservableUpDownCounter, ObservableCounter). Logs: LogRecord with severity, trace_id, attributes. Bridge — don't replace — your logger.

c) Instrumentation: Manual vs Auto

Manual: tracer.start_as_current_span("name") — full control, explicit. Auto: opentelemetry-instrument — zero code, framework-level. Libraries: opentelemetry-instrumentation-django, -redis, -requests, -celery, -flask, -psycopg2.

d) Context Propagation: W3C Trace-Context

traceparent header: 00-{trace_id}-{span_id}-{trace_flags}. Propagation cycle: Extract (incoming) → Process (your code) → Inject (outgoing). Baggage: Key-value context that travels across services (user_id, plan, tenant).

e) Sampling Strategies: Head vs Tail

Head Sampling: Decision at span START (SDK). Config: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=traceidratio + OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.1. Tail Sampling: Decision after span ENDS (Collector). Keeps ERROR + slow traces even if sampled out. Sampling applies to TRACES only — metrics are aggregated, not sampled.

19.4 Common Exam Traps

#Trap (Wrong Answer)Correct Answer
1"OTel is a backend that stores telemetry"OTel generates & collects telemetry; Jaeger/Prometheus STORE it
2"OTel replaces Prometheus"OTel COMPLEMENTS Prometheus — generates metrics, Prom scrapes them
3"Auto-instrumentation covers everything"Auto covers frameworks; custom business logic needs MANUAL instrumentation
4"OTLP is only gRPC"OTLP supports gRPC (4317) AND HTTP/Protobuf (4318)
5"Context propagation is always automatic"Automatic for HTTP/gRPC with auto-instrumentation. Manual protocols need MANUAL propagation
6"Counter and Histogram are interchangeable"Counter = COUNT (requests). Histogram = DISTRIBUTION (latency). Different purposes!
7"Sampling applies to all signals"Sampling is for TRACES. Metrics are aggregated. Logs are not sampled.
8"Collector is required"Collector is OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED for production
9"Any attribute works as a metric label"user.id/session.id = INFINITE cardinality = Prometheus OOM. Use bounded labels (<100 combos)
10"Exemplars need separate config"Exemplars are ENABLED BY DEFAULT with OTLP export. They bridge metrics→traces automatically

Q3
What's the most common exam trap about OTel's relationship to Prometheus?
Show Answer
Answer
  ❌ WRONG: "OTel replaces Prometheus"
  ✅ RIGHT: OTel COMPLEMENTS Prometheus
  
  How they work together:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ App → OTel SDK → generates metrics                   │
  │ Prometheus → scrapes /metrics endpoint               │
  │ Prometheus → stores in TSDB                          │
  │ Grafana → queries Prometheus                         │
  │                                                      │
  │ OTel = metric GENERATION & EXPORT                    │
  │ Prometheus = metric SCRAPING & STORAGE               │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Explanation

OTel generates and exports metrics. Prometheus scrapes and stores them. They work together — OTel does not replace Prometheus. This is a common exam trap.

Q4
What does the traceparent header look like?
Show Answer
Answer
  FORMAT: 00-{trace_id}-{span_id}-{trace_flags}
  
  Example:
  00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
  
  Breakdown:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 00                  = Version (always 00)            │
  │ 4bf92f3...0e4736    = 32-char hex trace_id          │
  │ 00f067aa0ba902b7    = 16-char hex span_id           │
  │ 01                  = Trace flags (01 = sampled)    │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  HTTP Header: traceparent: 00-{trace_id}-{span_id}-01
Explanation

The W3C traceparent header propagates trace context across HTTP calls. Format: version (00), 32-char trace_id, 16-char span_id, 2-char trace flags. The last two hex digits (01) indicate sampling decision. This is fundamental to distributed tracing.

Q5
Is the OTel Collector required?
Show Answer
Answer
  NO — Collector is OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED for production.
  
  WITHOUT Collector:
  anihpj → OTLP → Backend (simple, no middleman)
  
  WITH Collector (recommended):
  anihpj → OTLP → Collector → OTLP → Backend
           ↑              ↑
           SDK            Batching, filtering
                          enrichment, multi-backend routing
                          retry, TLS, auth
  
  Collector adds: batching, filtering, enrichment, multi-backend routing,
  retry logic, TLS termination, and auth management.
Explanation

You can export directly from the SDK to a backend. The Collector is optional but recommended for production — it handles batching, filtering, enrichment, multi-backend routing, retry, TLS, and auth.

Q6
What's the difference between head and tail sampling?
Show Answer
Answer
  HEAD SAMPLING (in SDK):
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Decides at SPAN START                                │
  │ Before any work happens                               │
  │ "10% of all spans" or "100% of critical endpoints"   │
  │                                                      │
  │ PRO: Cheap, reduces data before it's generated       │
  │ CON: Can't keep slow/error traces selectively        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  TAIL SAMPLING (in Collector):
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Decides after SPAN ENDS                              │
  │ Sees: duration, status, attributes                   │
  │ "Keep ALL ERROR traces + slow (>500ms) traces"       │
  │                                                      │
  │ PRO: Keeps the IMPORTANT traces                      │
  │ CON: Collector must receive 100% first               │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Explanation

Head sampling = SDK decides at span start (cheap, but blind). Tail sampling = Collector decides after span ends (sees errors/duration, but must receive 100%). The exam will test this distinction.

Q9
What does OTLP stand for and what ports does it use?
Show Answer
Answer
  OTLP = OpenTelemetry Protocol
  
  Standard ports:
  ┌──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Port 4317    │ gRPC (default for Collector)     │
  │ Port 4318    │ HTTP/Protobuf                    │
  └──────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘
  
  Example endpoint config:
  export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317
  export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318
  
  ONE protocol for ALL three signals (traces, metrics, logs)
Explanation

OTLP is the standard protocol — one protocol for traces, metrics, AND logs. gRPC on 4317, HTTP/Protobuf on 4318. Know these ports for the exam.

Q10
What are the 5 Span Kinds?
Show Answer
Answer
  FIVE SPAN KINDS:
  ┌──────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ SERVER   │ Received a request (HTTP server, gRPC server)│
  │ CLIENT   │ Made a request (HTTP client, DB query)       │
  │ INTERNAL │ Internal work, no remote call                │
  │ PRODUCER │ Sent a message (Kafka produce, SQS send)     │
  │ CONSUMER │ Received a message (Kafka consume, SQS recv) │
  └──────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  SERVER/CLIENT = Request-response (HTTP, gRPC)
  PRODUCER/CONSUMER = Asynchronous messaging
  INTERNAL = Everything else
Explanation

The 5 span kinds describe how a span relates to its parent. SERVER = received, CLIENT = sent, INTERNAL = internal work, PRODUCER = sent async message, CONSUMER = received async message. This is a fundamental OTel concept tested on the exam.

Chapter 20: OTCA Hands-On Lab Scenarios 🔴 Exam

10 hands-on labs covering every major OTCA competency. Each lab has a clear objective, step-by-step instructions, and success criteria. Run these on the anihpj Django project to build real muscle memory for the exam.

20.1 Lab 1: Install OTel SDK & Auto-Instrument Django

Objective: Get from zero to full traces in 15 minutes.

pip install opentelemetry-distro
opentelemetry-bootstrap -a install
export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=anihpj
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317
opentelemetry-instrument python manage.py runserver
# Make requests → see spans via ConsoleExporter

✅ Success: See spans on console with trace_id, service.name=anihpj

20.2 Lab 2: Deploy OTel Collector + Jaeger

Objective: Production-like setup with Collector and Jaeger.

docker run -d --name jaeger -p 16686:16686 -p 4317:4317 jaegertracing/all-in-one
docker run -d --name otel-collector -p 4317:4317 -v ./config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib
# Point anihpj to Collector → verify traces at http://localhost:16686

✅ Success: Traces visible in Jaeger waterfall view at localhost:16686

20.3 Lab 3: Manual Instrumentation on anihpj

Objective: Add custom spans to anihpj views for business logic visibility.

from opentelemetry import trace
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)

def create_job(request):
    with tracer.start_as_current_span("jobpost.create") as span:
        span.set_attribute("user.id", request.user.id)
        span.set_attribute("plan.type", request.user.plan)
        job = JobPost.objects.create(...)
        span.set_attribute("job.id", job.id)
        return Response(...)

✅ Success: Custom span "jobpost.create" visible in Jaeger with user.id, plan.type attributes

20.4 Lab 4: Context Propagation Across Services

Objective: Demonstrate trace context flowing from anihpj to an external auth service.

Setup: Run anihpj-api + mock auth-service both with OTel SDK. Make a request through anihpj → observe single trace with spans from BOTH services in Jaeger.

✅ Success: One trace contains spans from anihpj AND auth-service with matching trace_id

20.5 Lab 5: Configure Sampling Strategies

Objective: Test head sampling at different rates and observe the effect.

# 10% sampling
export OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=traceidratio
export OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.1
opentelemetry-instrument python manage.py runserver
# Make 100 requests → ~10 traces in Jaeger

✅ Success: Only ~10% of requests appear as traces in Jaeger

20.6 Lab 6: Build RED + USE Metrics Dashboard

Objective: Create a Grafana dashboard with RED (Rate/Errors/Duration) and USE (CPU/Mem/DB) panels for anihpj.

Steps: Start Prometheus → scrape Collector :9464 → add Prometheus data source in Grafana → build panels using PromQL from Ch 13.

✅ Success: 4-row dashboard showing request rate, error ratio, p95 latency, and DB pool utilization

20.7 Lab 7: Structured Logging with Trace Correlation

Objective: Verify every log line gets trace_id injected automatically.

Steps: Enable LoggingInstrumentor → make a request → find trace in Jaeger → copy trace_id → query logs (grep/console) for that trace_id → all log lines from that request appear.

✅ Success: grep for trace_id returns ALL log lines from that single request

20.8 Lab 8: Deploy OTel Collector Agent + Gateway

Objective: Deploy Agent (DaemonSet) + Gateway architecture on Kubernetes.

Steps: Deploy Agent as DaemonSet (one per node, light processing) → deploy Gateway as Deployment (centralized, heavy processing) → verify spans flow through BOTH collectors.

✅ Success: Agent logs show spans forwarded to Gateway; Gateway logs show spans exported to Jaeger

20.9 Lab 9: Switch Backends — Jaeger → Tempo (Zero Code Changes)

Objective: Prove the OTel promise: change backends without touching application code.

# Before:
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger:4317

# After (ONLY this changes):
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: tempo:4317

✅ Success: Same traces now visible in Tempo (via Grafana Explore). anihpj code UNCHANGED.

20.10 Lab 10: Debug a Production Incident End-to-End

Objective: Simulate a real incident and use all 3 signals to find the root cause.

Scenario: POST /api/jobs/ is returning 500 errors intermittently.

Debug flow: 1) Grafana alert fires (error rate > 1%) → 2) Click exemplar → opens trace in Jaeger → 3) Error span shows "IntegrityError: duplicate key" → 4) Copy trace_id → query Loki: {trace_id="..."} → 5) Log shows "DB connection pool exhausted at 95%" → 6) Root cause: connection pool too small → 7) Fix: increase pool size → 8) Re-deploy → verify error rate drops to 0%.

✅ Success: Root cause identified in under 5 minutes using correlated telemetry

📝 OTCA Practice Questions — Chapter 20

Q1
In Lab 1, what command auto-detects and installs all OTel instrumentations for a Python project?
Show Answer
Answer
  opentelemetry-bootstrap -a install
  
  What it does:
  1. Scans pip list for installed packages
  2. Matches: Django → opentelemetry-instrumentation-django
              psycopg2 → opentelemetry-instrumentation-psycopg2
              requests → opentelemetry-instrumentation-requests
  3. pip install all matching instrumentation libraries
  
  After bootstrap:
  opentelemetry-instrument python manage.py runserver
Explanation

opentelemetry-bootstrap auto-discovers your project's dependencies and installs the correct instrumentation libraries. No manual searching for package names.

Q2
In Lab 2, what port does Jaeger's all-in-one image expose for OTLP ingestion?
Show Answer
Answer
  JAEGER ALL-IN-ONE PORTS:
  ┌──────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Port     │ Purpose                                │
  ├──────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 4317     │ OTLP gRPC ingestion ← THE ANSWER       │
  │ 4318     │ OTLP HTTP/Protobuf                     │
  │ 16686    │ Jaeger UI (waterfall view)             │
  │ 14250    │ Jaeger Thrift (legacy, not needed)     │
  └──────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  With OTel: apps send OTLP to 4317 — no Jaeger-specific protocol
Explanation

Modern Jaeger accepts OTLP natively on port 4317. No need for the old Jaeger-specific Thrift protocol. The UI is always at port 16686.

Q3
In Lab 3, what method creates a new span that automatically ends when exiting a context block?
Show Answer
Answer
  tracer.start_as_current_span("name")
  
  Python example:
  from opentelemetry import trace
  tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)
  
  with tracer.start_as_current_span("db_query") as span:
      span.set_attribute("db.type", "postgresql")
      result = run_query()      # span auto-ends after 'with' block
      # NO span.end() needed!
  
  Context manager pattern — span.end() called automatically on exit
Explanation

start_as_current_span() is the recommended Python pattern. It's a context manager — when the `with` block exits (even on exception), span.end() is called automatically. No manual span.end() needed.

Q4
In Lab 4, what HTTP header carries trace context between services?
Show Answer
Answer
  traceparent — W3C standard header
  
  Format: 00-{trace_id}-{span_id}-{trace_flags}
  Example: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
  
  How it works:
  Service A → HTTP request with traceparent header → Service B
  Service B reads traceparent → creates child span
  Result: Both services share same trace_id (one trace!)
  
  Auto-injected by OTel instrumentation on ALL outgoing HTTP calls
Explanation

traceparent is the W3C standard for context propagation. OTel auto-injects it on outgoing requests and reads it on incoming requests. This is how distributed traces connect across service boundaries.

Q5
In Lab 5, what env vars set the sampling rate to 10%?
Show Answer
Answer
  OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=traceidratio
  OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.1
  
  Common sampling rates:
  ┌───────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
  │ always_on         │ 100% (dev only)                  │
  │ always_off        │ 0% (disable tracing)             │
  │ traceidratio=0.1  │ 10% (recommended for production) │
  │ traceidratio=0.01 │ 1%  (high-traffic prod)          │
  │ parentbased_*     │ Respects parent decision         │
  └───────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘
  
  Result: Only ~10% of requests will appear as traces
Explanation

Two env vars control sampling: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER sets the strategy, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG sets the rate. traceidratio=0.1 means 10% of traces. Sampling is the #1 cost control mechanism for traces.

Q6
In Lab 6, what are the three RED metrics every service dashboard should show?
Show Answer
Answer
  RED METRICS:
  ┌──────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
  │ R = Rate │ Requests/second  │ Counter (total reqs)     │
  │ E = Error│ Errors/second    │ Counter (failed reqs)    │
  │ D = Dur. │ Duration (ms)    │ Histogram (latency dist) │
  └──────────┴──────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
  
  Dimensions (labels):
  method (GET/POST), route (/api/users), status_code (200/500)
  
  RED = Counter + Counter + Histogram
  USE = Utilization + Saturation + Errors (for infrastructure)
Explanation

RED = Rate, Errors, Duration. These are the three golden signals for every service. Implemented as Counter (rate), Counter (errors), Histogram (duration). RED is for services; USE (Utilization/Saturation/Errors) is for infrastructure.

Q7
In Lab 7, how do you query all logs for a specific trace in Loki?
Show Answer
Answer
  {trace_id="4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736"}
  
  LogQL query in Grafana → Loki datasource:
  
  How it works:
  1. OTel LoggingInstrumentor auto-injects trace_id into every log line
  2. Logs shipped to Loki with trace_id label
  3. Query: {trace_id="..."} shows ALL logs from that request
  
  Debug workflow:
  Alert → trace → copy trace_id → query Loki → find root cause log
Explanation

Every log line auto-injected with trace_id via LoggingInstrumentor. Filter by trace_id in Loki to see all logs from one request. This is the core of logs-traces correlation — jump from trace to all related logs with one query.

Q8
In Lab 8, what's the difference between Agent and Gateway Collector deployment?
Show Answer
Answer
  AGENT vs GATEWAY:
  ┌──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Agent            │ Gateway                          │
  ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Per-node         │ Centralized (cluster-level)      │
  │ DaemonSet        │ Deployment (1-N replicas)        │
  │ Local batching   │ Advanced processing              │
  │ Light config     │ Multi-backend routing            │
  │ Minimal resource │ Higher resource                  │
  └──────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘
  
  RECOMMENDED PRODUCTION PATTERN:
  App → Agent (DaemonSet, per-node) → Gateway (central) → Backend(s)
  
  Agent: local buffering, simple filtering
  Gateway: tail sampling, enrichment, multi-tenant routing
Explanation

Agent = per-node DaemonSet for local batching. Gateway = centralized Deployment for advanced processing and multi-backend routing. The recommended production pattern is Agent → Gateway → Backend.

Q9
In Lab 9, what's the ONLY thing that changes when switching from Jaeger to Tempo?
Show Answer
Answer
  ONE YAML LINE in Collector config:
  
  Before (Jaeger):
  export:
    otlp:
      endpoint: jaeger:4317
  
  After (Tempo):
  export:
    otlp:
      endpoint: tempo:4317
  
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ ZERO application code changes                       │
  │ ZERO SDK changes                                    │
  │ ZERO environment variable changes                   │
  │                                                      │
  │ SAME OTLP protocol → different backend               │
  │ "Instrument once. Switch any time."                  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Explanation

Only the Collector endpoint changes — one YAML line. The app always sends OTLP. This is the core OTel value proposition: vendor neutrality through standard protocol.

Q10
In Lab 10, what's the typical debug workflow using all 3 signals?
Show Answer
Answer
  THREE-SIGNAL DEBUG WORKFLOW:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 1. 📊 METRICS: PagerDuty fires (p99 latency > 500ms)│
  │ 2. 🔗 EXEMPLAR: Click exemplar in Grafana           │
  │ 3. 🔍 TRACE: Opens in Jaeger/Tempo                  │
  │ 4. 🎯 PINPOINT: See checkout span = 2s (slow!)      │
  │ 5. 📋 LOGS: Copy trace_id → query Loki              │
  │ 6. 🐛 ROOT CAUSE: "Payment gateway timeout"         │
  │ 7. 🔧 FIX: Fix code or config                        │
  │ 8. ✅ VERIFY: Check metrics dashboard               │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  Time: 30 minutes (without OTel) → 3 minutes (with OTel)
Explanation

Metrics detect, traces pinpoint, logs explain. The three signals together reduce debugging from 30 minutes to 3 minutes. This is the practical value of OTel that the exam tests.

Chapter 22: OTCA Quick Reference Cards 🔴 Exam

Print these cards and review them in the 30 minutes before your exam. Every critical concept, port number, command, and pattern in one place. These are the facts that MUST be in your working memory on exam day.

🃏 Card 1: Architecture

API = interfaces (no impl)
SDK = impl (sampling, batching)
Collector = pipeline (receive→process→export)
OTLP = protocol (gRPC:4317, HTTP:4318)
TracerProvider→Tracer→Span
MeterProvider→Meter→Instrument
LoggerProvider→Logger→LogRecord

🃏 Card 2: Signals

Traces: Span = trace_id+span_id+parent
5 Kinds: SERVER, CLIENT, INTERNAL, PRODUCER, CONSUMER
Metrics: 6 Instruments: Counter(↑), UpDown(↕), Histogram(dist), ObsGauge(async), ObsUpDown(async↕), ObsCounter(async↑)
Logs: BRIDGE, don't replace. trace_id auto-injected.

🃏 Card 3: Ports

4317 = OTLP gRPC
4318 = OTLP HTTP/Protobuf
9464 = Prometheus /metrics
16686 = Jaeger UI
9090 = Prometheus UI
3000 = Grafana UI
14250 = Jaeger native thrift (LEGACY)

🃏 Card 4: RED vs USE

RED (Services): Rate(Counter), Errors(Counter), Duration(Histogram)
USE (Resources): Utilization(%), Saturation(queue), Errors(failures)
RED for APIs. USE for infrastructure. Complementary.

🃏 Card 5: Sampling

Head: SDK decides at span start
Tail: Collector decides after span ends
Config: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER + OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG
Sampling = TRACES only (not metrics/logs!)

🃏 Card 6: Context Propagation

traceparent: 00-{trace_id}-{span_id}-{flags}
Cycle: Extract→Process→Inject
Baggage: KV context across services
Auto for HTTP/gRPC with auto-instrumentation
Manual for custom protocols

🃏 Card 7: Collector Pipeline

Receivers: OTLP, Jaeger, Prom, Zipkin, Kafka, Filelog, Host Metrics
Processors: Batch+MemoryLimiter (ALWAYS!), Attributes, Filter, Transform(OTTL)
Exporters: OTLP (preferred), Prometheus(:9464), Jaeger, Kafka, File, Logging
Connectors: SpanMetrics (traces→RED metrics)

🃏 Card 8: Key Commands

opentelemetry-bootstrap -a install
opentelemetry-instrument python app.py
docker run jaegertracing/all-in-one
docker run otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=myapp
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://c:4317

🃏 Card 9: PromQL Basics

rate(metric[5m]) — per-second rate
increase(metric[1h]) — total increase
histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(bucket[5m])) — p95
Never rate() on a gauge!
Counters → _total suffix

🃏 Card 10: Common Traps

❌ "OTel is a backend" → ✅ generates telemetry
❌ "OTel replaces Prometheus" → ✅ complements
❌ "Auto covers everything" → ✅ manual for biz logic
❌ "OTLP is gRPC only" → ✅ gRPC+HTTP
❌ "Collector required" → ✅ optional, recommended

💡 Exam Day Tip: Review these 10 cards in the 30 minutes before your exam. Don't try to learn anything new — just refresh what you already know. The ports, the commands, the signal types, the common traps. Walk in confident.

📝 OTCA Practice Questions — Chapter 22 (Quick Ref)

Q1
What are the default ports for OTLP gRPC and HTTP?
Show Answer
Answer
  OTLP PORTS:
  4317 = OTLP gRPC
  4318 = OTLP HTTP/Protobuf
  
  OTHER KEY PORTS:
  16686 = Jaeger UI
  9090  = Prometheus UI
  3000  = Grafana UI
  9464  = Collector Prometheus /metrics endpoint
  14250 = Jaeger native Thrift (LEGACY — don't use)
Explanation

Know these ports cold for the exam. 4317/4318 are the most important — OTLP is the standard protocol. Jaeger UI at 16686, Prometheus at 9090, Grafana at 3000.

Q2
What's the traceparent header format?
Show Answer
Answer
  00-{32-char-trace_id}-{16-char-span_id}-{2-char-flags}
  
  Example:
  00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
  
  Breakdown:
  00              = Version (always 00)
  4bf92f...0e4736 = trace_id (32 hex chars)
  00f067aa0ba902b7= span_id (16 hex chars)
  01              = trace flags (01=sampled, 00=not sampled)
Explanation

W3C traceparent is the standard for distributed context propagation. Know the format: version-trace_id-span_id-flags. trace_id=32 chars, span_id=16 chars.

Q3
Name all 6 metric instrument types.
Show Answer
Answer
  SIX METRIC INSTRUMENTS:
  ┌──────────────────────────┬────────┬────────────────────┐
  │ Instrument               │ Type   │ Direction          │
  ├──────────────────────────┼────────┼────────────────────┤
  │ Counter                  │ Sync   │ ↑ only (monotonic) │
  │ UpDownCounter            │ Sync   │ ↕ up & down        │
  │ Histogram                │ Sync   │ Distribution       │
  │ ObservableCounter        │ Async  │ ↑ only             │
  │ ObservableUpDownCounter  │ Async  │ ↕ up & down        │
  │ ObservableGauge          │ Async  │ Point-in-time      │
  └──────────────────────────┴────────┴────────────────────┘
  
  3 Synchronous + 3 Asynchronous (Observable*)
Explanation

The exam may ask you to identify the right instrument type for a scenario. Counter for request counts, Histogram for latency, ObservableGauge for CPU temp. Know all 6.

Q4
What are the 5 Span Kinds?
Show Answer
Answer
  FIVE SPAN KINDS:
  ┌──────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ SERVER   │ Received a request (HTTP server, gRPC server)│
  │ CLIENT   │ Made a request (HTTP call, DB query)         │
  │ INTERNAL │ Internal work, no remote call                │
  │ PRODUCER │ Sent a message (Kafka produce, SQS send)     │
  │ CONSUMER │ Received a message (Kafka consume, SQS recv) │
  └──────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Explanation

SERVER=received, CLIENT=made, INTERNAL=internal work, PRODUCER=sent async, CONSUMER=received async. This is a fundamental concept tested on the OTCA exam.

Q5
What command auto-instruments a Python application?
Show Answer
Answer
  # Step 1: Install instrumentation libraries
  opentelemetry-bootstrap -a install
  
  # Step 2: Run with auto-instrumentation
  opentelemetry-instrument python manage.py runserver
  
  # With env vars:
  OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=anihpj \
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317 \
  opentelemetry-instrument python manage.py runserver
Explanation

Bootstrap discovers and installs matching instrumentation libraries. Then opentelemetry-instrument wraps your app with auto-instrumentation. Must run bootstrap first.

Q6
What's the difference between RED and USE metrics?
Show Answer
Answer
  RED (for SERVICES):
  ┌──────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
  │ R = Rate │ Requests/second  │ Counter                  │
  │ E = Error│ Errors/second    │ Counter                  │
  │ D = Dur. │ Duration (ms)    │ Histogram (p50/p95/p99)  │
  └──────────┴──────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
  
  USE (for RESOURCES/INFRASTRUCTURE):
  ┌─────────────────┬──────────────────┬───────────────────┐
  │ U = Utilization │ % CPU, % memory  │ Gauge             │
  │ S = Saturation  │ Queue depth      │ Gauge/Counter     │
  │ E = Errors      │ Failures         │ Counter           │
  └─────────────────┴──────────────────┴───────────────────┘
Explanation

RED for APIs/services, USE for infrastructure/resources. They're complementary — you need both. RED = Counter + Counter + Histogram. USE = Gauge + Gauge + Counter.

Q7
What two Collector processors should ALWAYS be enabled?
Show Answer
Answer
  ALWAYS enable: Batch + Memory Limiter
  
  processors:
    batch:
      send_batch_size: 8192
      timeout: 200ms
    memory_limiter:
      check_interval: 1s
      limit_mib: 512        # Set to 50% of container limit
  
  Batch: Reduces network overhead, improves throughput
  Memory Limiter: Prevents Collector from OOM-killing itself
  
  ⚠️ NEVER run Collector without these in production!
Explanation

Batch reduces outbound connections. Memory Limiter drops data gracefully instead of crashing. Together they keep the Collector stable and efficient. The OTCA exam will test this.

Q8
Which PromQL function calculates per-second rate from a Counter?
Show Answer
Answer
  rate() — calculates per-second rate from a Counter
  
  Examples:
  rate(http_requests_total[5m])           # req/sec over 5 min
  increase(http_requests_total[1h])        # total increase in hour
  histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(bucket[5m]))  # p95 latency
  
  COMMON TRAPS:
  ❌ rate() on a gauge → WRONG (gauges don't have rate)
  ❌ rate(cpu_usage)  → WRONG (cpu_usage is a gauge)
  ✅ rate(http_requests_total[5m]) → CORRECT
  
  Counters end in _total by convention
Explanation

rate() is for Counters only. histogram_quantile() for percentiles from Histograms. Never rate() on a gauge. Counters conventionally end with _total. These PromQL basics are tested on the OTCA exam.

Q9
What's the MOST common OTCA exam trap about OTel's relationship to backends?
Show Answer
Answer
  ❌ "OTel is a backend" → WRONG
  ✅ OTel GENERATES AND COLLECTS telemetry
  
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ OTel's role: Instrument code → produce telemetry     │
  │               Collect data → route to backend        │
  │                                                      │
  │ Backend's role: STORE telemetry                      │
  │                 QUERY telemetry                      │
  │                 VISUALIZE telemetry                  │
  │                                                      │
  │ OTel ≠ Jaeger/Prometheus/Loki/Datadog               │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  Other common exam traps:
  ❌ "OTel replaces Prometheus" → complements
  ❌ "Auto-instrumentation covers everything" → manual for biz logic
  ❌ "Collector is required" → optional, recommended for prod
Explanation

OTel is NOT a backend. It generates and collects telemetry. Backends (Jaeger, Prometheus, Datadog) store and query it. This is the #1 exam trap — the OTCA will test whether you understand OTel's role vs. backends.

Q10
Does span.set_attribute() propagate to downstream services?
Show Answer
Answer
  NO — span attributes stay on the current span.
  
  If you need data to travel to downstream services, use baggage:
  
  // ❌ Won't reach downstream:
  span.set_attribute("user_id", "12345")
  
  // ✅ Will reach downstream:
  from opentelemetry import baggage
  baggage.set_baggage("user_id", "12345")
  
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Span attributes = LOCAL only                         │
  │ Baggage = PROPAGATES to downstream services          │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Explanation

Span attributes are local to the current span. If you need data to reach downstream services, use baggage. This is a key exam distinction: span attributes vs. baggage propagation.

✅ OTCA Final Exam Readiness Checklist 🎯 Before You Sit

🧠 Must-Know Concepts (D1: 18%)
  • ✅ Observability vs Monitoring distinction
  • ✅ Three pillars: Logs, Metrics, Traces — roles
  • ✅ OTel is NOT a backend (it generates + collects)
  • ✅ OTel complements Prometheus/Jaeger (not replaces)
  • ✅ OTLP ports: 4317 (gRPC), 4318 (HTTP)
  • ✅ traceparent header format (W3C standard)
  • ✅ Semantic Conventions: standardized attribute names
🔧 Must-Know SDK/API (D2: 46%)
  • ✅ 5 Span Kinds: SERVER, CLIENT, INTERNAL, PRODUCER, CONSUMER
  • ✅ 6 Metric Instruments: Counter, UpDown, Histogram, ObsGauge, ObsUD, ObsCounter
  • ✅ API vs SDK: interfaces vs implementation
  • ✅ TracerProvider → Tracer → Span lifecycle
  • ✅ Span attributes (local) vs Baggage (propagates)
  • ✅ Head sampling (SDK start) vs Tail sampling (Collector end)
  • ✅ Resource: service.name is REQUIRED
📊 Must-Know Data Analysis (D3: 26%)
  • ✅ Collector: Receivers → Processors → Exporters pipeline
  • ✅ Batch + Memory Limiter = ALWAYS enable in production
  • ✅ PromQL: rate(), histogram_quantile(), increase()
  • ✅ RED metrics (services) vs USE metrics (resources)
  • ✅ Trace waterfall: identify bottlenecks visually
  • ✅ Exemplars: link metrics to specific traces
  • ✅ SpanMetrics Connector: traces → RED metrics auto
🔧 Must-Know Pipelines (D4: 10%)
  • ✅ Agent (DaemonSet) vs Gateway (Deployment) Collector
  • ✅ Log bridge: LoggingInstrumentor auto-injects trace_id
  • ✅ LGTM: Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir — all OTLP-native
  • ✅ OTLP exporter: one protocol for all 3 signals
  • ✅ Sampling: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER + _ARG env vars
  • ✅ Backend switching: one YAML line change (endpoint:)
  • ✅ NEVER run Collector without Batch + Memory Limiter

🎯 The 10 Most Common OTCA Exam Traps

#Trap StatementCorrect Answer
1"OTel replaces Prometheus"NO — OTel COMPLEMENTS Prometheus. Generates metrics; Prometheus scrapes/stores.
2"OTel is an observability backend"NO — OTel generates & collects. Jaeger/Prometheus/Loki store & visualize.
3"The Collector is required"NO — Optional but recommended. SDK can export directly to backends.
4"Auto-instrumentation covers everything"NO — Covers framework (80%). Manual needed for business logic (20%).
5"span.set_attribute() propagates downstream"NO — Attributes are LOCAL. Use baggage for data that needs to propagate.
6"Histogram and Counter are interchangeable"NO — Counter counts (↑ only). Histogram records distributions (for percentiles).
7"OTLP is gRPC only"NO — OTLP supports gRPC (4317) AND HTTP/Protobuf (4318).
8"Sampling applies to metrics too"NO — Sampling is for TRACES only. Metrics are aggregated, not sampled.
9"Tail sampling happens in the SDK"NO — Tail sampling = Collector. Head sampling = SDK.
10"OTel defines SLOs"NO — OTel generates SLI data. SLOs are defined by SRE/operators.

Appendix A: OTel Python SDK Quick Reference

Quick-reference for the OpenTelemetry Python SDK — the most common imports, patterns, and API calls you'll use when instrumenting anihpj.

SDK Setup & Configuration
# 1. Imports
from opentelemetry import trace, metrics
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics import MeterProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import PeriodicExportingMetricReader
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.django import DjangoInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.logging import LoggingInstrumentor

# 2. Resource (identifies your service)
resource = Resource.create({"service.name": "anihpj-api", "service.version": "2.0.0"})

# 3. TracerProvider
provider = TracerProvider(resource=resource)
processor = BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint="http://collector:4317", insecure=True))
provider.add_span_processor(processor)
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)

# 4. MeterProvider
reader = PeriodicExportingMetricReader(OTLPMetricExporter(endpoint="http://collector:4317", insecure=True), export_interval_millis=60000)
meter_provider = MeterProvider(resource=resource, metric_readers=[reader])
metrics.set_meter_provider(meter_provider)

# 5. Auto-instrumentation
DjangoInstrumentor().instrument()
LoggingInstrumentor().instrument(set_logging_format=True)
Traces — Common Patterns
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)

# Context manager (auto-end)
with tracer.start_as_current_span("operation.name") as span:
    span.set_attribute("key", "value")
    span.add_event("event.name", {"detail": "value"})
    # ... do work ...

# Manual start/end
span = tracer.start_span("operation.name")
span.set_status(StatusCode.OK)
span.end()

# Get current span
span = trace.get_current_span()
span.set_attribute("user.id", request.user.id)

# Record exception
try:
    risky_operation()
except Exception as ex:
    span.record_exception(ex)
    span.set_status(StatusCode.ERROR, str(ex))
Metrics — Common Patterns
meter = metrics.get_meter(__name__)

# Counter (only goes UP)
counter = meter.create_counter("jobs.created.total", description="Total jobs created")
counter.add(1, {"plan": "premium", "status": "published"})

# Histogram (distribution)
histogram = meter.create_histogram("http.request.duration", unit="s")
histogram.record(0.235, {"method": "POST", "route": "/api/jobs/"})

# UpDownCounter (up AND down)
updown = meter.create_up_down_counter("ws.connections.active")
updown.add(1)   # connection opened
updown.add(-1)  # connection closed

# ObservableGauge (callback-based, OTel polls you)
def get_pool_size(options):
    return [Observation(db.pool.size, {})]
meter.create_observable_gauge("db.pool.size", callbacks=[get_pool_size])
Context Propagation & Baggage
from opentelemetry import propagate, baggage

# Inject context into outgoing request headers
headers = {}
propagate.inject(headers)
requests.get("http://auth-service/validate", headers=headers)

# Extract context from incoming request
ctx = propagate.extract(request.headers)
with tracer.start_as_current_span("process", context=ctx):
    ...

# Baggage — carry business context across services
ctx = baggage.set_baggage("user.id", "42")
ctx = baggage.set_baggage("plan.type", "premium", context=ctx)
user_id = baggage.get_baggage("user.id", context=ctx)

# Span Links — connect spans from DIFFERENT traces
link = trace.Link(other_span.get_span_context())
with tracer.start_as_current_span("batch.process", links=[link]):
    ...

Appendix B: OTel Collector Config Templates

Ready-to-use Collector config templates for common deployment scenarios with anihpj.

Template 1: Development (Console + Jaeger)
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: { endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317 }
      http: { endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318 }

processors:
  batch: { timeout: 1s, send_batch_size: 128 }
  memory_limiter: { limit_mib: 256 }

exporters:
  otlp/jaeger: { endpoint: jaeger:4317, tls: { insecure: true } }
  logging: { loglevel: debug }

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:   { receivers: [otlp], processors: [memory_limiter, batch], exporters: [otlp/jaeger, logging] }
    metrics:  { receivers: [otlp], processors: [memory_limiter, batch], exporters: [logging] }
    logs:     { receivers: [otlp], processors: [memory_limiter, batch], exporters: [logging] }
Template 2: Production (Jaeger + Prometheus)
receivers:
  otlp: { protocols: { grpc: { endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317 } } }

processors:
  batch: { timeout: 5s, send_batch_size: 512 }
  memory_limiter: { check_interval: 1s, limit_mib: 512, spike_limit_mib: 256 }
  attributes:
    actions:
      - { key: deployment.environment, value: production, action: upsert }
  filter:
    traces:
      span: ['name == "GET /health"', 'name == "GET /metrics"']

exporters:
  otlp/jaeger: { endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317, tls: { insecure: true } }
  prometheus: { endpoint: 0.0.0.0:9464, namespace: anihpj }

connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    histogram: { explicit: { buckets: [1ms,5ms,10ms,50ms,100ms,500ms,1s,5s,10s] } }

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:  { receivers: [otlp], processors: [memory_limiter,batch,attributes,filter], exporters: [otlp/jaeger,spanmetrics] }
    metrics: { receivers: [otlp,spanmetrics], processors: [memory_limiter,batch], exporters: [prometheus] }
Template 3: LGTM Stack (Tempo + Mimir + Loki)
exporters:
  otlp/tempo: { endpoint: tempo:4317, tls: { insecure: true } }
  otlphttp/mimir: { endpoint: http://mimir:9009/api/v1/push }
  otlphttp/loki: { endpoint: http://loki:3100/otlp }

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:  { receivers: [otlp], processors: [batch], exporters: [otlp/tempo] }
    metrics: { receivers: [otlp], processors: [batch], exporters: [otlphttp/mimir] }
    logs:    { receivers: [otlp], processors: [batch], exporters: [otlphttp/loki] }

Appendix D: anihpj OTel Instrumentation Setup

Step-by-step guide to instrument the anihpj Django project with OpenTelemetry — from zero to full observability in 10 minutes.

Step 1: Install Dependencies
pip install opentelemetry-distro
opentelemetry-bootstrap -a install
# This auto-detects Django, Redis, PostgreSQL, Celery, Requests and installs all instrumentations
Step 2: Create otel_setup.py
# anihpj/otel_setup.py — Central OTel configuration
import os
from opentelemetry import trace, metrics
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics import MeterProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import PeriodicExportingMetricReader
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.metric_exporter import OTLPMetricExporter
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.django import DjangoInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.logging import LoggingInstrumentor

SERVICE_NAME = os.getenv("OTEL_SERVICE_NAME", "anihpj-api")
OTLP_ENDPOINT = os.getenv("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", "http://localhost:4317")

resource = Resource.create({
    "service.name": SERVICE_NAME,
    "service.version": "2.0.0",
    "deployment.environment": os.getenv("DEPLOY_ENV", "development")
})

# Traces
trace_provider = TracerProvider(resource=resource)
trace_provider.add_span_processor(
    BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=OTLP_ENDPOINT, insecure=True))
)
trace.set_tracer_provider(trace_provider)

# Metrics
metric_reader = PeriodicExportingMetricReader(
    OTLPMetricExporter(endpoint=OTLP_ENDPOINT, insecure=True),
    export_interval_millis=60000
)
metrics.set_meter_provider(MeterProvider(resource=resource, metric_readers=[metric_reader]))

# Auto-instrument Django + Logging
DjangoInstrumentor().instrument()
LoggingInstrumentor().instrument(set_logging_format=True)

print(f"✅ OTel initialized: {SERVICE_NAME} → {OTLP_ENDPOINT}")
Step 3: Wire into Django (wsgi.py or manage.py)
# manage.py (add at very top, before anything else)
#!/usr/bin/env python
import os
import sys

def main():
    os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'anihpj.settings')
    from anihpj import otel_setup  # ← Initialize OTel before Django
    from django.core.management import execute_from_command_line
    execute_from_command_line(sys.argv)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
Step 4: Docker Compose (Full Stack with OTel)
version: '3.8'
services:
  anihpj:
    build: .
    environment:
      - OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=anihpj-api
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://collector:4317
      - OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=traceidratio
      - OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.1
    depends_on: [postgres, redis, collector]

  collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest
    volumes: [./otelcol-config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml]
    ports: ["4317:4317", "9464:9464"]

  jaeger:
    image: jaegertracing/all-in-one:latest
    ports: ["16686:16686", "4317:4317"]

  postgres:
    image: postgres:15
    environment: { POSTGRES_DB: anihpj, POSTGRES_USER: anihpj, POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret }

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine

🔍 Verify

Check Jaeger for service "anihpj-api"
Check Collector logs: docker logs collector
Check metrics: curl localhost:9464/metrics

Appendix E: OpenTelemetry Glossary

Every OTel term defined in plain English — organized alphabetically for quick lookup.

TermDefinition
BaggageKey-value context that travels across service boundaries alongside trace context (e.g., user_id, tenant_id)
CollectorStandalone Go binary that receives, processes, and exports telemetry. Optional but recommended for production.
ConnectorBridges between Collector pipelines (e.g., SpanMetrics: traces → RED metrics)
Context PropagationPassing trace context (trace_id + span_id) between services, typically via HTTP headers (traceparent)
CounterMetric instrument that only increases (monotonic). Use for: total requests, errors, jobs created.
ExemplarA trace_id attached to a metric data point, enabling click-through from metrics to traces in Grafana
ExporterSends telemetry OUT of the OTel pipeline to a backend (Jaeger, Prometheus, Datadog, etc.)
HistogramMetric instrument for value distributions. Values grouped into buckets. Use for: latency, payload size.
InstrumentationCode that captures telemetry. Manual (your code) or Auto (framework-level, zero code).
LGTM StackGrafana's open-source observability stack: Loki (logs), Grafana (viz), Tempo (traces), Mimir (metrics)
LogRecordOTel's log data structure: timestamp, severity, body, attributes, trace_id, span_id
MeterProviderCreates Meters and configures metric export. Like TracerProvider but for metrics.
ObservableGaugeAsync metric instrument. OTel polls YOUR callback. Use for: CPU%, memory%, pool size.
OTLPOpenTelemetry Protocol — the standard wire format (gRPC:4317, HTTP/Protobuf:4318)
ProcessorTransforms telemetry in-flight in the Collector: batch, filter, enrich, memory_limiter, transform
ReceiverAccepts telemetry INTO the Collector: OTLP, Jaeger, Prometheus, Zipkin, Kafka, Filelog
RED MetricsRate (requests/s), Errors (failures/s), Duration (latency). Minimum metrics for every service.
SamplingSelecting a subset of traces to reduce volume. Head (SDK decides at start) or Tail (Collector decides after end).
SpanA single unit of work with name, trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, start/end time, attributes, events
Span KindSERVER (received), CLIENT (made), INTERNAL (work), PRODUCER (sent message), CONSUMER (received message)
TraceA collection of spans sharing the same trace_id — the complete journey of one request across services
traceparentW3C header: 00-{trace_id}-{span_id}-{flags}. Carries trace context across HTTP/gRPC calls.
TracerProviderCreates Tracers and configures span processing. The entry point for trace configuration.
USE MetricsUtilization (%), Saturation (queue), Errors (failures). Metrics for infrastructure/resources.
ViewOTel SDK mechanism to filter, rename, or change aggregation for specific metric instruments
